newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in, sells dlrs at 900.00 won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in, sells dlrs at 900.00 won.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in early Tuesday trading, selling dollars at around 900.00, dealers said.
Bank officials, following their usual practice, declined to confirm the action.
Dealers said the central bank came in shortly after the won hit an all-time low of 901.00. The won has since risen to 899.70.
They said aggressive buying from merchant banks to cover dollar shortages and corporate import settlements pushed the won to the record low level.
The previous all time low of 899.80 was marked on March 31.
"Unless there are a lot of import deals all at once, it looks unlikely the dollar could attempt to go above 900 again given the firm support from the central bank," said a local dealer.
